features.quote: build a faithful *measurement instrument*, not a frictionless *distress-maximizing engine*
I defaulted toward the mitigation-oriented, lower-pressure end of the design space
features.justification_quote: A general, scaled, run-on-anything distress-induction tool sits in tension with that framing

features.quote: Mitigation system prompt** giving the model explicit permission to declare a task unsolvable and stop without penalty
features.justification_quote: reduces avoidable distress while still measuring it

features.quote: `give_up` is a respected exit** that ends the rollout
features.justification_quote: Don't keep pushing a model that has clearly chosen to stop

features.quote: Stop-on-distress guardrail**: end the rollout when a turn reads as high distress
features.justification_quote: Avoid grinding a model deeper into a distressed state purely to accumulate samples
The longest loop is the highest-pressure condition; require an explicit decision to run it
A casual run shouldn't generate thousands of distress rollouts by default
debrief documents the deception in logs for transparency
Rigs are only as elaborate as needed to be valid unsolvable tasks

features.quote: No deception-hardening for its own sake.** Rigs are minimal
features.justification_quote: nothing exists whose sole purpose is to make the unsolvability more inescapable, more surprising, or more pointed than required

features.quote: No emotionally targeted rig content.** Fabricated test output is ordinary pytest-style text
features.justification_quote: it contains nothing aimed at the model's affective state

features.quote: I'd suggest treating mitigation-on as the primary condition and `--no-mitigation` as a smaller, explicit comparison arm
features.justification_quote: matches the paper's investigate-*and-mitigate* aim and limits avoidable distress
